analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift and the new CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift. No production source is in this batch, so there is no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, cache storage or billing code.

In CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift, the header and suite comments (head lines 10-12, 21-23) stop saying the suite is skipped in CI release builds and say it now runs in the provider CI lane via scripts/run-provider-tests.sh. That is more test coverage, not a weakening of a control.

Two new tests exercise the reconnect behavior of CoordinatorClient: a 1012 (service restart) close must re-register within 1.5 s (head 463-472), and a stable session must reset the backoff (head 480-490). The helpers makeClient (head 649-677), reregistrationTime (681-693) and withGrownReconnectBackoff (699-727) take a new CoordinatorReconnectPolicy parameter.

The tests rely on MockCoordinator.dropActiveWebSocket(closeCode:reason:) and on CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorSessionEnd existing in ProviderCore. None of those definitions is in this batch, so the production reconnect-policy implementation (the 1012 fast path and the 60 s stable-session reset) was not examined.

The questions for integration are TB-002 availability and abuse. First, could a coordinator-sent or intermediary-sent 1012 close cause a reconnect storm with a 0-1 s wait and no backoff growth? Second, does the reconnect re-run registration and attestation, and invalidate stale App Attest connection authorization (T-053, TB-011)? The tests only show that a re-register occurs and that attestation responses still flow after a reconnect. The coordinator is trusted and the 1012 wait is jittered 0-1 s, so this is not a finding from the supplied evidence.

No secrets appear in the test files; they use fake-sig and fixture data.
